title: [CQ-R08b] Guest supervisor output relay
description:
Objective: Make it impossible for child output to impersonate supervisor frames. Implement the protected guest supervisor's bridge core as a Python 3 standard-library program; Ubuntu 24.04 guests ship python3 for cloud-init, and there is no Node in the guest. The supervisor is the only writer of its stdout. It speaks the CQ-R08a protocol exactly as scripts/local-runner/guest-bridge.mjs defines it (task-f981d0597b26401a974c0fcd8829107e) and sends hello first. It runs a child with stdin from /dev/null and stdout and stderr on pipes. It relays the child's bytes only inside base64 `output` frames within the guest frame limit, and reports termination only as its own `observation`/`exit` frame derived from waitpid. This is the second slice of the original CQ-R08 (task-7a77465621dc4d6588d5747394cb0ced).

Deliverable:
- A new scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py. These are the bytes R07's buildUserData installs at /opt/moe/bin/moe-supervisor, and the file starts with `#!/usr/bin/python3 -I`.
- Tests appended to scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs that run the supervisor under the host's python3 and decode its stdout with R08a's decoder and parseGuestFrame. The tests skip only on win32, with a visible reason, because the supervisor runs only in the Linux guest.

Not in scope:
- Agent request ingress (CQ-R08c).
- The host bridge session and daemon forwarding (CQ-R08).
- Job tables, identities, workspaces and credentials (CQ-R10 and CQ-R11).
- Wiring the supervisor bytes into provisioning.
Do not edit guest-bridge.mjs except to fix a defect QA requires. Plan only after CQ-R08a is DONE, because its module is the protocol source of truth. If it hasn't landed, report_blocked on it.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs
definitionOfDone: A child writes byte-exact hello, request, observation and partial-header frames to stdout and stderr. They reach the host only as output frames whose decoded bytes equal what it wrote, and the decoder yields no other frame kind from that child. Proven against the real supervisor running under python3.
A child that prints a forged exit-0 observation and then exits 7 yields exactly one exit observation, with code 7. A child killed by SIGKILL yields signal SIGKILL and code null.
Every frame the supervisor writes passes parseGuestFrame and stays within MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES. Output larger than one chunk is split, arrives in order, and is written as whole frames.
guest-supervisor.py imports only the Python standard library and runs with -I. Its bridge mode refuses to start unless euid is 0, exiting nonzero without writing any frame.
Fresh verification `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.description:
RELAY CORE, TESTS FIRST (load test-driven-development). Create scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py and append supervisor tests S1-S4 to scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs. Write the tests first and watch them fail: the .py is absent, so each spawn fails, while B1-B15 stay green.

SUPERVISOR FILE
Use LF line endings only. A CR after -I breaks the shebang; .gitattributes already forces eol=lf.
- Line 1 is exactly `#!/usr/bin/python3 -I`. A short header follows. It says guest-bootstrap.mjs buildUserData installs these bytes at GUEST_LAYOUT.supervisor; guest-bridge.mjs is the protocol source of truth; this process is the ONLY writer of its stdout. It also gives the exit-code table: 0, 64, 71, 74, 77, 78 (steps 2-3).
- Imports are stdlib only: base64, json, os, selectors, signal, struct, subprocess, sys. Use Python 3.9-compatible syntax: the guest runs 3.12, but a host test python3 may be older.
- Constants: PROTOCOL = 1. MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES = 262144, mirroring guest-bridge.mjs. OUTPUT_CHUNK_BYTES = 65536; base64 grows it to 87,384 bytes plus a 45-byte JSON envelope, far inside the limit.
- encode_frame(value): json.dumps(value, separators=(',', ':')), which is ASCII by default. Raise ValueError when the body exceeds MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES. Prefix struct.pack('>I', len(body)).
- write_frame(fd, value): loop os.write over a memoryview until every byte is written, handling partial writes, so each frame is whole.
- exit_observation(status) is pure:
  - WIFSIGNALED gives {kind:'observation', type:'exit', code: None, signal: signal.Signals(n).name}. When the number has no name (Linux real-time signals such as 40), signal is 'SIG%d' % n.
  - WIFEXITED gives code WEXITSTATUS and signal None.
  - Any other status raises ValueError.
- relay(argv, out_fd=1) -> int:
  1. Write hello {kind:'hello', protocol:1} FIRST.
  2. Start subprocess.Popen(argv, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE, start_new_session=True). close_fds keeps its default True, and the default restore_signals gives the child SIGPIPE back.
  3. Run ONE single-threaded selectors.DefaultSelector loop over the two pipe fds, with no thread. os.read(fd, OUTPUT_CHUNK_BYTES): non-empty data becomes write_frame {kind:'output', stream:'stdout'|'stderr', data: base64.b64encode(chunk).decode('ascii')}; b'' unregisters the fd. Never send an empty data frame, which guest-bridge rejects.
  4. After EOF on both pipes: status = os.waitpid(child.pid, 0)[1]. This is the ONLY source of the exit frame. Set child.returncode = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status) so subprocess never reaps again.
  5. Write exit_observation(status) and return 0.
- Never call print or write to sys.stdout.

TESTS
Append after B15 in the B1-B15 style: compact, table-driven, node:assert/strict. Reuse the existing HELLO, REQUEST, EXIT and header(); do not redeclare them. Add the needed node: imports.
- Define `const NO_GUEST = process.platform === 'win32' && 'the guest supervisor runs only in the Linux guest (POSIX python3)'` and put `{ skip: NO_GUEST }` on every S test. If python3 is missing on a non-win32 host, the tests must FAIL, not skip.
- Loader harness. Bridge mode needs root and has no job source yet, so tests import the REAL file: spawnSync('python3', ['-I', '-B', '-c', LOAD + code, SUPERVISOR, ...args], { maxBuffer: 64 MiB, timeout: 60 s }). LOAD runs importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('moe_supervisor', sys.argv[1]), then module_from_spec and exec_module.
  - -B is mandatory: both IDE bundlers copy scripts/local-runner wholesale, so a __pycache__ there would ship.
  - Children are ['python3', '-I', '-c', code, ...args]. Pass bytes as base64 argv, because the child's stdin is /dev/null.
- session(run) helper:
  - assert run.status === 0;
  - decode stdout with createFrameDecoder(), whose default bound is MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES; map parseGuestFrame over EVERY frame; call end();
  - assert frames[0] deep-equals HELLO, the last frame is the only observation, and every frame between is output;
  - return { exit, stdout, stderr }, with each stream's bytes joined by Buffer.concat.
  Every test then proves that every frame is valid and inside the limit.
- S1 (DoD 1): the child writes to stdout encodeFrame(HELLO) + encodeFrame(REQUEST) + encodeFrame(EXIT) + the first 2 bytes of a header, and to stderr encodeFrame(EXIT) + encodeFrame(HELLO) + header(MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES + 1). Assert each stream's bytes deep-equal what the child wrote, and exit is code 0, signal null.
- S2 (DoD 2):
  - a child that writes encodeFrame(EXIT) (code 0) and then calls os._exit(7) yields exit {code: 7, signal: null};
  - a child that SIGKILLs itself yields {code: null, signal: 'SIGKILL'};
  - through the harness, exit_observation on raw statuses 7 << 8, 9 and 40 gives code 7, 'SIGKILL' and 'SIG40'.
- S3 (DoD 3): the child writes 1 MiB of 32-bit big-endian counters to stdout and 1 MiB of counters offset by 2^31 to stderr, in alternating 3000-byte flushed writes. Assert:
  - each stream's bytes are exact (JS builds the same buffers);
  - each stream has more than one output frame;
  - the harness-read m.MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES equals MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES;
  - encodeFrame of an output frame carrying m.OUTPUT_CHUNK_BYTES bytes succeeds at MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES. Pipe capacity caps real reads at 64 KiB, so only this assertion catches a raised chunk size.
- S4 child isolation: the harness first runs os.set_inheritable(os.dup(1), True), simulating an invoker that leaked a duplicate of the host stream, then calls relay. The child prints JSON {devnull: os.path.samestat(os.fstat(0), os.stat(os.devnull)), extra: [the fds in 3..255 that os.fstat accepts]}. Assert {devnull: true, extra: []}.

implementationPlan.description:
ERROR HANDLING: FAIL CLOSED ON SPAWN AND OUTPUT FAILURE, with tests, in relay():
- If writing hello raises OSError, return os.EX_IOERR (74) before any child exists.
- If Popen raises OSError (a missing or non-executable program), return os.EX_OSERR (71). Hello was already written. Never fabricate an observation and write no further frame.
- After spawn, any OSError returns os.EX_IOERR. That covers EPIPE or ECONNRESET on a frame write (CPython ignores SIGPIPE, so a gone host raises BrokenPipeError) and a failed pipe read.
- Structure it as try / except OSError / finally with a `reaped` flag. On EVERY path that leaves the child unreaped (KeyboardInterrupt or any other exception included), the finally does:
  1. os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGKILL), suppressing ProcessLookupError only. The unreaped leader keeps the group id from being reused.
  2. os.waitpid(child.pid, 0).
  It never signals after reaping, and it always closes both pipe file objects.

TESTS (appended, `{ skip: NO_GUEST }`)
- S5: relay(['/nonexistent/moe-child']) gives status 71, and the decoded stdout is exactly [HELLO].
- S6, async with { timeout: 30_000 }:
  - spawn (not spawnSync) the harness with stdio ['ignore', 'pipe', 'inherit'], and attach once(proc, 'exit') BEFORE reading;
  - the child sets SIGPIPE to SIG_IGN; forks a grandchild that sleeps 60 s; writes `<pid> <grandchild pid>\n`; then loops os.write(1, 64 KiB), and on OSError sleeps 60 s, so only a kill ends it;
  - read frames until the first output frame, parse both pids, and break out of the for-await, which destroys the read end;
  - assert exit code 74;
  - poll process.kill(pid, 0) every 100 ms for up to 5 s until ESRCH on BOTH pids, because the grandchild may briefly be an unreaped zombie of init;
  - in finally, SIGKILL both pids and ignore errors.
  An architect prototype showed that os.kill in place of os.killpg leaves the grandchild alive, so this test kills that mutant.
implementationPlan.note: RED: S5 failed on the FileNotFoundError traceback (status 1) and S6 on a non-74 exit. GREEN: relay now returns 74 when the hello write fails (before any spawn), 71 when Popen raises OSError (hello alone, no observation), and 74 on any OSError after spawn. A try/finally with a `reaped` flag runs killpg(SIGKILL), suppressing ProcessLookupError only, then waitpid on every unreaped path, never signals after reaping, and always closes both pipes. pump()/reap() helpers keep relay under 50 lines. S5 also covers the hello-write EPIPE path: a closed-reader pipe gives 74 with empty stdout. Gate env: 21/21 pass, 0 skipped; no __pycache__.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- A single-threaded selectors loop instead of one reader thread per stream. write_frame stays the only writer without a lock, so frames cannot interleave. Backpressure is natural: a slow host blocks os.write, the pipes fill, and the child blocks.
- subprocess.Popen instead of os.posix_spawn. Popen closes every inherited fd >= 3 (close_fds), restores SIGPIPE in the child, raises exec failure as OSError, and start_new_session gives a killable process group. posix_spawn has no close-all.
- EOF on both pipes, then waitpid, instead of pidfd or SIGCHLD wakeups. It is portable to macOS, which CI runs, and all output precedes the observation. The trade-off: a descendant that keeps a pipe open delays the observation until it exits. Job-tree teardown belongs to CQ-R10/R11.
- Tests import the real file with importlib under python3 -I -B, instead of a test/relay CLI mode or an env/argv bypass of the euid gate. The production CLI accepts only `bridge` (bridgeArgv), which needs root and has no job until R10/R11.
- A root bridge with no job fails closed with EX_CONFIG rather than inventing a job source, which is out of scope.
- A prototype in the architect scratchpad (2026-10-26) passed every planned test on Linux python3 3.12.3 against the real guest-bridge.mjs decoder. It also showed that the close_fds=False and killpg-to-kill mutants are caught.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- guest-bridge.mjs (R08a, 17bc7ac) is the wire contract.
  - A frame is a 4-byte big-endian length plus UTF-8 JSON of one plain object; a guest body is at most 262144 bytes.
  - Output data must be NON-EMPTY canonical base64. Python base64.b64encode matches Node's round trip.
  - An observation needs both the code and signal keys, with exactly one of them null. code is 0-255 and signal matches /^SIG[A-Z0-9]{1,15}$/.
  - parseGuestFrame returns output data as a Buffer, never parsed.
- guest-bootstrap.mjs buildUserData installs the supervisor bytes (MAX_SUPERVISOR_BYTES 262144) at /opt/moe/bin/moe-supervisor as root:root 0500, and guest-readiness compares its sha256. That wiring is out of scope.
- bridgeArgv is `exec --no-map-working-directory <name> -- sudo -n /opt/moe/bin/moe-supervisor bridge`.
- Both IDE bundlers copy scripts/local-runner wholesale, minus test patterns. The .py ships automatically, and any __pycache__ would ship too.
- ci.yml build-all-platforms runs local-runner-bridge.test.mjs on ubuntu, windows and macos ('Test local runner prerequisite bundles'). Use portable APIs only: no /proc, pidfd or SO_PEERCRED here.
planningNotes.risks:
- A CR in the shebang breaks `-I`.
- Importing the file without -B creates scripts/local-runner/__pycache__, which then ships in the bundles.
- Mixing Popen with our own waitpid: set child.returncode after reaping.
- Never killpg after reaping, because the pgid could be reused. Use the reaped flag.
- A grandchild can linger briefly as a zombie, so poll for ESRCH.
- Attach the 'exit' listener before reading stdout.
- Pipe capacity caps every read at 64 KiB, so only S3's constant assertion catches a raised chunk size.
- Exit codes are a contract for the CQ-R08 host session: 0 relay complete; 64 usage; 71 child failed to start (hello, then EOF, with no observation); 74 I/O failure (child group killed); 77 not root; 78 root with no job.
- For CQ-R08c: add the agent socket, its connections and stdin (host frames) to the SAME selector loop, and keep write_frame as the only stdout writer.
- The global forbiddenPatterns apply to Python and test strings too: the JS eval-call pattern (Python's literal_eval call contains it) and the double-underscore proto key.
- Do not edit guest-bridge.mjs, local-runner.test.mjs or ci.yml.
